messages.content: Let's start a separate trip for my spouse and me. We have six nights for the Maine coast in September and want to divide them between Portland and Bar Harbor.
What dates are you considering, and will you be flying from Denver? Also, do you want exactly two full days available for Acadia, apart from the arrival and departure days?
September 13 through 19, from Denver. Yes, two genuinely full Acadia days. We will share one room the whole trip, though obviously in two hotels.

That is Saturday through Friday, six hotel nights. The main routing choices are round trip through Portland, Portland inbound with Bangor outbound, or the reverse open jaw. Portland to Bar Harbor is about three hours of driving without a substantial stop; Bangor airport is roughly 75 minutes from Bar Harbor. Do you want Portland at the beginning or end, or should the flight and hotel combination decide it?
Let the combination decide. I don't want to discover that a sensible flight order leaves us with only one real park day.

Then I would compare three complete sequences. First: two Portland nights followed by four Bar Harbor nights, flying into Portland and out of Bangor. Second: four Bar Harbor nights followed by two Portland nights, using Bangor inbound and Portland outbound. Third: Portland round trip, with two nights there first and four in Bar Harbor, accepting the long drive back to Portland on departure day. Each sequence can preserve two full park days, but the third is vulnerable if the Friday flight leaves early.
Can you put actual days against those? I am losing track of which nights go where.

Sequence A: Portland Saturday and Sunday nights; drive to Bar Harbor Monday; stay Monday through Thursday nights; use Tuesday and Wednesday as full Acadia days; fly from Bangor Friday. Sequence B: Bar Harbor Saturday through Tuesday nights; use Sunday and Monday as full park days; drive to Portland Wednesday; stay Wednesday and Thursday nights; fly from Portland Friday. Sequence C follows A's hotel order, but on Friday you drive about three hours from Bar Harbor to Portland before the flight.
A and B both sound workable. Is Bangor realistic from Denver, or does it create an ugly itinerary?

Bangor normally means a connection, while Denver-Portland may have a nonstop on some schedules. The open jaw is still realistic because Bangor removes roughly two hours of Maine driving compared with returning to Portland from Bar Harbor. For A, the best fit would be a Friday Bangor departure no earlier than late morning. For B, the Bangor arrival should be early enough to collect a car and reach Bar Harbor before dinner. Live schedules and fares would need checking for these exact dates.
I would rather connect on the way home than arrive late and then drive in the dark. So A is ahead. What about splitting Portland three nights and Bar Harbor three nights?

A three-and-three split works on paper, but it is weaker for Acadia. You would reach Bar Harbor Tuesday and have only Wednesday and Thursday as the protected full days before Friday's airport trip. Any weather disruption would consume half the park time. Two Portland nights and four Bar Harbor nights gives you Tuesday and Wednesday for Acadia, Thursday as a spare park or coastal day, and an easier Friday departure from Bangor.
Keep the two-and-four split. Show me a few lodging combinations, but not luxury resorts. One room for two adults, and quote totals rather than making the nightly rates do all the work.

For a practical comparison, I would price three pairings for September 13-19: a central Portland hotel such as the Hyatt Place Portland-Old Port paired with the Acadia Hotel-Downtown in Bar Harbor; the Hampton Inn Portland Downtown-Waterfront paired with the Bar Harbor Manor; and a less central Portland option such as the Cambria Hotel Portland Downtown paired with the Atlantic Eyrie Lodge. The first two Bar Harbor properties support walking into town; Atlantic Eyrie generally trades that convenience for a quieter hillside setting. Availability and six-night all-in totals must be checked live.
The first two sound more useful. We may not want to move the car every evening in Bar Harbor. How should I judge the Portland side?

For only two Portland nights, compare the final room total plus parking, not just the room rate. Hyatt Place and Hampton Inn both put the Old Port and waterfront within walking distance. Hampton is slightly farther from the densest part of the Old Port but can be straightforward for getting back onto the road Monday. Confirm the exact parking charge, cancellation deadline, and whether the quoted room has one king or queen bed rather than two doubles.
And in Bar Harbor, Acadia Hotel versus Bar Harbor Manor?

Acadia Hotel-Downtown is the stronger town-centered choice if a suitable room is available for all four consecutive nights. Bar Harbor Manor is also walkable but sits a little farther from the waterfront core. Compare one-room totals for Monday, September 15 through Friday, September 19, including taxes and any parking or resort fees. Because those four nights are the tighter part of the trip, I would confirm Bar Harbor availability before treating either Portland pairing as viable.
Suppose Acadia Hotel only has three consecutive nights. Could we stay Sunday through Wednesday there and rearrange everything?

You could, but that would force either a one-night move in Bar Harbor or a three-night Portland allocation. A cleaner response would be to test the reverse sequence: Bar Harbor Saturday through Tuesday and Portland Wednesday through Thursday. However, that requires the Saturday Bangor arrival you already found less attractive. I would first look for four continuous nights at Bar Harbor Manor before changing the route.
Agreed. Give me the strongest primary plan and one fallback, including the drives and which days remain fully open for Acadia.

Primary plan: fly Denver to Portland on Saturday, September 13; stay two nights at Hyatt Place Portland-Old Port or Hampton Inn Portland Downtown-Waterfront; drive to Bar Harbor on Monday, September 15, allowing about three hours plus any stop; stay four nights at Acadia Hotel-Downtown, with Bar Harbor Manor as the same-sequence substitute; reserve Tuesday and Wednesday as full Acadia days; use Thursday as a flexible additional coast or park day; drive about 75 minutes to Bangor on Friday, September 19, and return to Denver with a connection. This is the best balance of arrival ease and protected park time.
What is the fallback if the four-night Bar Harbor rooms are the problem?

Fallback: fly Denver to Bangor on Saturday only if an itinerary arrives early enough for the drive before dark; stay four nights at either Bar Harbor property from Saturday through Tuesday; keep Sunday and Monday fully open for Acadia, with Tuesday as the flexible extra day; drive roughly three hours to Portland on Wednesday; stay there Wednesday and Thursday; then fly Portland to Denver Friday. This avoids splitting the Bar Harbor stay, though it makes the outbound flight timing critical.
That is enough. Finish with exactly what needs to be checked before we choose, and leave it all unbooked.

Check the primary sequence first: Denver-Portland on Saturday, September 13, followed by two Portland nights; four consecutive Bar Harbor nights from Monday, September 15 through Friday, September 19; and Bangor-Denver on Friday. Verify live flight times, connection length, baggage terms, rental-car pricing with pickup at Portland and return at Bangor, and that the Friday departure leaves enough time for the roughly 75-minute drive plus fuel and airport check-in. For lodging, compare all-in totals and refundable terms for Hyatt Place versus Hampton Inn in Portland and Acadia Hotel-Downtown versus Bar Harbor Manor in Bar Harbor, confirming one shared room for two adults, the bed type, parking cost, and four-night continuity. Keep Tuesday and Wednesday untouched as the two full Acadia days. Use the reverse Bangor-to-Portland sequence only if the Saturday arrival permits a comfortable daylight drive and materially improves the four-night Bar Harbor availability or total cost. Nothing has been booked.
